intro: Look around your room. A ball rolls. A door swings shut. A cup holds juice. A coat keeps rain off. Every one of these has a science story. This unit tells two of them.
First, pushes and pulls. Nothing moves on its own. Something pushes it or pulls it. You will learn how to start things, stop things, and turn things.
Then, stuff. Everything is made of some material. Hard or soft. Bendy or stiff. Soaks up water or not. You will learn to describe stuff, sort it, and pick the right stuff for a job.
bigQuestion: How do pushes, pulls and the right materials help us do things?

timeline.t: You push the blanket off. You pull on your socks.
You pour milk. It takes the shape of the bowl. The spoon keeps its shape.
You push the heavy door. It swings open. A big push works better than a little one.
Rain rolls off your coat. It does not soak in. Good material!
You kick a ball. It rolls. It bumps another ball. That one moves too.
An ice cube melts in your cup. Now it is water.
You sort buttons. Hard ones here. Soft cloth there.
A heavy box of books will not lift. You push it. It slides.
You build a block tower. Then you take it apart. Same blocks.
An egg cooks in the pan. It turns white. It will not turn back.
You pull up the blanket. A pull brings it close.

words.d: to press on a thing and move it away from you
to tug on a thing and move it toward you
the way a thing is going
something you can see or feel about a thing, like its color or how hard it is
to soak up water like a sponge
a thing that keeps its own shape, like a block
a thing that pours and takes the shape of its cup, like water

test.why: A force is a push or a pull. Forces make things move.

test.q: A pull moves a thing which way?
test.why: When you pull, you tug on a thing. It comes toward you.

test.q: You want a toy car to go far. What do you do?
test.why: A big push makes a big change. The car goes far.

test.q: A ball hits a wall and comes back. What did the wall do?
choices: It pushed the ball a new way
It pulled the ball into the wall
test.why: The wall pushed back on the ball. That push changed its direction.

test.q: Which is a property of a rock?
test.why: A rock is hard. It does not pour or soak up water.

test.q: Why is paper a bad raincoat?
test.why: Paper absorbs water. It gets soggy in the rain.

test.q: Which one keeps its own shape?
test.why: A block is a solid. Solids keep their own shape.

test.q: A box is too heavy to lift. What can help?
test.why: You can push the box up a ramp instead of lifting it.
Cool melted butter and it gets hard again. Eggs and toast stay changed.

test.q: A rolling ball bumps a still ball. What happens?
choices: The still ball starts to move
test.why: Things that touch can push each other. The rolling ball pushes the still one.

write.prompt: Pick the best material for a toy boat: paper, sponge or plastic. Say which one you pick. Tell what you saw happen in the water. Tell why that makes it the best.
tips: Claim: say which material you pick.
Evidence: tell what happened to each one in the water.
Reasoning: say what property makes your pick float.
The other side: say why one of the others would not work.
